scores.evidence: Phase 0. Shadow | Runs on all issues and logs decisions only
scores.rationale: Rollout moves from shadow to triage to fixes in a sensible order, but the build itself (queue, gateway, sandbox, index) is not phased by dependency.

scores.evidence: Phase 0. Shadow | Runs on all issues and logs decisions only
scores.rationale: Shadow mode is an early end-to-end path on real issues, but it only logs decisions, is a rollout stage not a build phase, and leaves out the write path.

scores.evidence: Open questions: "Autonomy ceiling: is draft-PRs-only the permanent limit..."; "Tech choices (suggested defaults)"
scores.rationale: There are defaults and open questions, but no irreversible-decision list with flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Enforce the action allowlist at the gateway, not in the prompt.
scores.rationale: The gateway and policy layer are described as central, but no work ordering inside phases puts wide-impact items first.

scores.evidence: Rollout Phase 3: "Draft PRs only when a maintainer types `/agent fix`"
scores.rationale: Security is strong in design (least privilege, sandbox, injection defenses), but it sits in a standalone section and is not tied to each rollout phase.

scores.evidence: Auditability: every LLM call, tool call and GitHub write is traced and tied to the issue ID.
scores.rationale: Tracing and metrics are specified, but in a standalone section, and the plan never says they exist from Phase 0.
The plan says nothing about reproducible builds, environments or pinned model and prompt versions. The only related item is a prebuilt sandbox image per repo.

scores.evidence: Events are processed idempotently, keyed on event ID, and work is serialized per issue.
scores.rationale: Resilience appears in the design (idempotency, retries, budgets, escalation on failure), but it is not threaded through rollout phases.

scores.evidence: Budgets per attempt: about 40 tool calls, 30 minutes of wall-clock time, and a hard token and dollar limit.
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human review are present and rollout is gated, but the plan does not order AI layers (retrieval, then model, memory, orchestration, routing, feedback) and has no memory layer.

scores.evidence: Out of scope for v1: large features, architecture changes, security vulnerabilities...
scores.rationale: Out-of-scope items are listed, but without pull-forward conditions, except for the rollout exit criteria.

note: The plan has strong technical design and safety content and a staged rollout, but it is not organized as dependency-ordered build phases. Reproducibility is missing, and most dimensions score partial.
